quote_text:
It was a bit of a strange game start to finish.  Talk us through that from your perspective.
Uh, good comeback from our point of view.  Um, silly sending off. I spoke to young Ross  
about it. He understands that when you get  a yellow card, you can't make a—a challenge.
So I have no complaints about the second yellow.  
But maybe I should be looking at that when  he did get the first yellow. I was thinking  
in my mind that I maybe make a change.  But listen, I didn’t. Ross got sent off,  
and then you have to go and kind of—kind of  go back to what we done on Thursday night.
Had to make a few changes, um, at half-time,  and I thought the changes certainly kicked  
us on a bit. So yeah, overall I’m  never really happy drawing a game,  
but under the circumstances, we got to  get back down the road pretty pleased.
You made nine changes to your team  before the game. On the TV, contrary,  
Chris Sutton said that he could  understand why you were doing that,  
but it was like you were waving a white flag.  Do you feel that with a 95th-minute equaliser,  
playing right to the death with ten men, it proves  that you weren’t waving a white flag at all?
Look, I—I have no issue. Everybody has an  opinion. When people say things like that,  
I don’t really—I don’t really take interest.  I’ve got a decision to make. I’m carrying a  
lot of injuries. There was a number  of players having to be left behind.
There was actually a number of players  on the bench that probably I shouldn’t  
have had on the bench. So I’ve got decisions to  make as a manager. But the team that I put out,  
in my mind, in my opinion, was good enough to—to  come up here and try and get the three points.
Can you take spirit from that—that last-minute  
equaliser coming into the  massive game on Thursday?
Yeah, I’ll take spirit probably in a couple of  days if I get good news from the medical staff—if  
I’m going to have another three or four players  fit and available. I just need to wait and see.
But look, the one thing about them  is—I questioned it last week against,  
um, Hibs. I questioned the—the character  and the desire. We all know what happened  
on the Monday. Certainly the last two games,  they’ve showed that they’ve certainly got that.
We’ve got to play better, but we’ve got  to try and keep eleven men on the pitch.  
That’s becoming a—a recurring theme. So if we  have eleven men on the pitch, then I’ve got  
a better chance of winning games. But when you  get down to ten, I thought they stuck together.
Thought they worked ever so hard. You have  to surrender a lot of possession, but they  
were willing to do that. I said that—you have to  sacrifice that and hopefully we’ll get that couple  
of chances, and we got the couple of chances.  We obviously stuck them in the back of the net.
Will you be able to get some  of those injured players back?
Well, I think you can see who wasn’t in  the squad. So I just need to wait and see  
their reaction over the next couple of days  because we left straight after training. So,  
um, I’ll—I’ll find out  tomorrow, Tuesday at the latest.
But I’m not going to take any chances. I need  people who—you’re never 100% when you play games  
of football—but I need people as close to that  because we know how difficult it’s going to be.
Did you rest some today just because—
No, no. I always had it in my mind  because people have been chapping my  
door and asking me for an opportunity.  So they—they got an opportunity today.  
Wasn’t ideal when you go down to ten  men—it doesn’t suit some players.
So then I have to make the changes to  get midfielders in who are kind of used  
to being behind the ball. So no, I had—I had  it in my mind that I was going to make a—a  
few changes. Some were enforced, obviously  suffering a few injuries on Thursday night.
But that’s the reason why you—you carry a  squad. That’s the reason why I wanted to  
give some players the opportunity. It wasn’t  a case of coming up here and this was a—a dead  
game. It wasn’t a dead game in my mind. Just  coming up to Aberdeen—remember, you know what  
it’s like up here—I was coming up here to win.  And unfortunately, didn’t get that three points.
Young Curtis had a bit of a torrid  time in the first half against Morris,  
but I thought he did well...
I disagree with you. I  disagree. In the first half,  
I thought the young man was excellent.  I disagree that he had a tough time.
The second half, I thought he came on too.  I thought overall—I thought the full game,  
until I brought him off—I thought young Finlay  was—was, um, was really good. I must have been  
watching a different game, because I thought  the first half, the young man was—was excellent.
And as I’ve said before, you’ve got to remember  what age—they’ve not exposed them a lot. It’s  
not been a—a lot of exposure. And especially  coming to a—it’s intimidating at times. But  
I thought the young man—I was proud of  him today. Proud of him after the game.
And yourself, involved with—
Involved? No, I was just saying to Big Suits,  
“Just leave it. It’s pointless.”  So it was a bit of handbags.
So no, no—it’s—you know what it’s like. It’s  a bit feisty after the game. I don’t mind a—a  
bit of feisty things going on. But I just  told Big John just to leave it. What’s the  
point in getting involved with—with him? And  the big man just stepped away and that’s it.
But I—I have no issues with that.  People are passionate. I like to see  
a bit of passion. I think that’s something  that’s missing in the modern game at times.
What was the thinking behind  making McCrorie captain,  
and what did you make of the way he handled the  atmosphere—obviously getting a lot of abuse?
Yeah, listen, the wee man can  handle that. He knows what he  
was going to come in for in terms  of getting a bit of stick tonight.
And remember that he done a  very good job at Aberdeen. And,  
um, he was a good player for Aberdeen, hence  the fact that he wanted to better his career  
and go to Rangers. I thought  he handled the occasion well.
Obviously Tav coming on obviously takes the  band out of respect. But I thought the young  
man was—was really good today. He’s—he’s  brilliant to work with, young McCrorie.
He’s got some things in his game that he  understands he has to work at. And I think  
if he works at them and he gets better at them,  he’ll become a—an all-round better midfielder.
Looking ahead to Thursday now?
Huge. Can’t wait. I said to them there—we’re  going to have a rest tomorrow. And,  
um, I’m excited about going.  But I’m also respectful.
It’s going to be tough for us.  But as a footballer, as a manager,  
um, I’m excited about it. I’m—I’m excited  about getting into that sort of atmosphere.
And what an opportunity we’ve got.  The game’s wide open. Wide open.
The main thing for me on Thursday  night was making sure we were still  
in the tie. And the guys deserved, with  the performance, to still be in the tie.
And, um, we’ll go there on Thursday,  um, having to know our jobs and what  
way we’re going to play. ’Cause we need to get  it spot on. We do really need to get it spot on.
And that’s up to me and the  coaching staff to make sure we  
do over Tuesday and Wednesday before  we—we get into the game on Thursday.
Does that atmosphere crank up a bit?
Yep. Um, it—it does. But I—I look at the  last two games in terms of the last round,  
sorry, to get into the quarters—Fenerbahçe  
and now Athletic Club—they’re—they’re a  different—they’re a step up. They are.
I’m being honest. They’re a step up. I know Lyon,  
when—when we played them at home,  they were very good middle to front.
But it’s a step up. So we need to be bang  on the button with our tactics. I already  
know what way we’re going to approach it  and what way we’re going to go about it.
So there’s going to be a—a bit of work on  the training ground. But one thing about  
them is—I’ll give the boys, um, a lot of credit.  They’ve been brilliant taking information on.
Because it’s tough, because it’s a  different way that we’re playing tactically,  
um, and with—and without the ball as well.
We know there’s a lot of work to be  done. But we’ll—we’ll get there and  
we’ll be prepared, ready to go on Thursday night.
Thanks, guys. Cheers, guys.
title: Barry Ferguson FULL Post Match Interview | Aberdeen 2-2 Rangers
